items.title: Fix domestic arbitration before pursuing global arbitration hub ambitions: Justice L Nageswara Rao
items.summary: India must first address delays, court interference and the lack of confidence in its domestic arbitration system before seeking to become a global arbitration hub, former Supreme Court judge Justice L Nageswara Rao said on Saturday. Justice Rao was speaking at GHAC Arbitration Week 2026 , organised by the Gujarat High Court and the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. “ Unless we improve domestic arbitration, there is no point in thinking about international arbitration ,” he said. Justice Rao said India had fertile ground for disputes, with hundreds of thousands of arbitrations taking place in the country. However, there was no reliable data even on the number of pending ad hoc arbitrations. He noted that arbitration practitioners from London, Singapore and Dubai regularly came to India because of the volume of disputes available here. At the same time, Indian parties were choosing foreign seats to secure more efficient resolution. He said “ What does this indicate? items.title: Mere possession of book alleged to be anti-national is not ground for preventive detention: J&K High Court
items.summary: An academic being in possession of books alleged to be anti-national does not make him a criminal warranting his criminal detention, the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh held. Justice Moksha Khajuria Kazmi said that mere possession of books with “dispiriting titles” and authored by someone else is not sufficient to invoke preventive detention laws, particularly when the authorities fail to demonstrate any specific subversive or prejudicial activity attributable to the persons. The Court made the observation while quashing a preventive detention order issued under the Jammu & Kashmir Public Safety Act against academic scholar Shafat Maqbool Wani, who had been detained on the basis of allegations of involvement in anti-national activities and possession of alleged anti-national literature. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: ஆதாரம் இருந்தும் நடவடிக்கை எடுக்காத Chennai police! |Shabbir Ahmed |TNM Tamil
items.summary: A POCSO case in Chennai has raised serious questions about the investigation of sexual assault allegations involving a minor and the police's approach to protect the accused. The case took a dramatic turn after a Special POCSO Court rejected the police’s attempt to close the investigation and ordered further probe. The subsequent investigation led to the arrest of granite businessman R Veeramani and two associates, Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan. Police have alleged that several minor girls were brought to a house in Teynampet and that the couple helped facilitate the alleged offences. In this week’s episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the unanswered questions surrounding the case, the lapses in police investigation, the court’s intervention and the larger concerns it raises about accountability in offences involving children.

items.title: UN names November 27 as day against child marriage, nods to India’s campaign
items.summary: On September 4, the United Nations passed a resolution declaring November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. For India, the date holds significance. It was on this day in 2024 that the Union government launched its ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign against child marriage. About six months ago, in March 2026, Bhuwan Ribhu, founder of Just Rights for Children (JRC), addressed the United Nations, reiterating the call for a UN resolution to mark November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early, and Forced Marriage. Dr Fatima Maada Bio, First Lady of Sierra Leone, among other global leaders, supported the call. Sierra Leone subsequently led the effort, presenting a resolution to the UN General Assembly seeking the designation, with around 50 nations, including India, backing it. Ribhu, who was the only civil society representative present at the UN when the resolution was adopted, said: “The Child Marriage Free India campaign, which started first by the children and communities, has today become an International Day accepted by the world. items.title: YSRCP alleges TDP govt removed social media posts related to teacher recruitment scam
items.summary: The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has accused the TDP-led Andhra Pradesh government of censorship, alleging that several of its social media posts on the District Selection Committee (DSC) recruitment scam have been removed by the state through the Sahyog portal. According to the Opposition party, posts on Facebook and Instagram, including those published by Sakshi TV, the party’s mouthpiece, have been taken down. The YSRCP has alleged that the government is using the expanded online content-removal mechanism to suppress criticism of alleged irregularities in the state’s Mega DSC recruitment process. What is the DSC scam? Large-scale irregularities have been alleged in the recruitment process of teachers through the Mega DSC examination. While the TDP government had promised 25,000 teacher posts, the recruitment was eventually conducted for 16,347 posts. Nearly three lakh candidates appeared for the examination. According to the YSRCP, the examination paper was leaked. items.title: Judiciary acts like load-bearing wall in economic progress: CJI Surya Kant at BRICS Chief Justices’ Forum
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday said that judicial systems function like the load-bearing wall of a nation by providing the foundation for economic progress, technological development, dispute resolution and sustainable energy. CJI Kant made the comment while delivering the welcome address at the BRICS Chief Justices’ Forum hosted at the Supreme Court of India. "Our role, as representatives of the justice delivery system, is much like that of a load-bearing wall within a building. No architect ever photographs it for the brochure, and yet no building stands without it. That, precisely, is the place, judicial systems occupy in the life of a nation, ” the CJI said. CJI Surya Kant added that uncertainty over resolution of commercial dispute directly increases the cost of doing business. When foreign investors lack confidence in a country’s dispute-resolution system, contracts carry higher risk premiums, additional securities and stringent exit clauses, he said. “ It becomes, in every practical sense, an unwritten punitive cost of doing business, one that no legislature ever imposed, yet every investor ends up paying, ” the CJI added.
